facts.text: Anka found forbidden books and told Leonuka about them, leading Leonuka to bargain with a dark power to try to save the convent from the plague.
When Leonuka was one step away from ending the curse on the convent, Anka stopped her.
Anka decided to complete the ritual herself to atone for stopping Leonuka, and Cohen reluctantly agreed to let her do it alone.
Anka performed the ritual alone in the catacombs while Cohen waited in the library listening to inhuman sounds from the crypt.
After the ritual, Cohen found that the nuns of the convent had vanished.
Cohen and Anka found a book titled Sancti Mihi Histori Vera whose pages appeared blank, written in invisible ink.
The book Sancti Mihi Histori Vera reveals that Saint Mihi, believed by the valley's people to have fought dragons, actually fought the Verkieri.
According to the manuscript, Saint Mihi was a pagan who struck down a Verkier with a magically strengthened sword that cut through evil.
Saint Mihi's body was believed lost, but the manuscript claims he was buried with his belongings somewhere in Svartra.
Albertus was a monk who served as chronicler under Kinaz Brenis, tasked with praising the ruler's virtues and hiding his sins.
Albertus devoted his life to studying the history of Veil Sangora, but the Verkieri banished him and destroyed his life's work when they seized power.
After losing his research, Albertus reportedly went mad and now lives on the streets.
Anka admitted to Cohen that she has had feelings for him for a long time.
Cohen found Saint Mihi walled in alive beneath the cathedral in Svartra, emaciated but still breathing after centuries of imprisonment.
Saint Mihi mistook Cohen for a man named Tobias and attacked him with a broken sword.
After Cohen defeated him, Saint Mihi revealed that Tobias had betrayed and imprisoned him centuries earlier.
Saint Mihi called Cohen a 'dawn walker' and claimed to be one himself.
Tobias was a monk who believed Mihi was a pagan sorcerer and imprisoned him underground, fabricating the church legend of St. Mihi despite the good Mihi had done.
Saint Mihi's sword was shattered and its pieces were carried off by cobalts; Cohen would need to recover the fragments and have Yurashi blacksmiths reforge it.
Before dying, Saint Mihi promised Cohen that beings called 'the augers' would eventually find him and explain what a dawn walker truly is.
Father Floren, the priest who preaches at the blood masses, sent soldiers to an ancient shrine of St. Mihi, leading Cohen to investigate the cobalt caves.
Cohen found cave drawings made by cobalts depicting Mihi as a monstrous warrior who slaughtered many cobalts before being defeated by a lone cobalt hero who shattered his sword.
The cobalts divided Mihi's shattered sword among three nests, treating each fragment as a sacred relic.
Cohen killed Brenis's soldiers who had raided the third cobalt cave and recovered the final sword fragment.
A Yurashi blacksmith agreed to reforge Mihi's sword for free once she learned Cohen intended to kill Brenis.
Cohen empowered the reforged sword with nameless magical power inside an ancient ruin in the mountains, making it deadly against both humans and monsters.
Ambress, one of Brenis's boyers, challenged Cohen to a one-on-one duel at a ruined fortress near Maragir.
In Maragir, villagers celebrated Ambress's execution of former nobility by crucifixion, and feared Cohen as the Verkier-hunting dawn walker.
Julen Codrin, a noble who swore loyalty to Ambress on the night the Verkieri seized power, secretly wanted Ambress dead.
Ambress kept a private herd of humans to feed on despite Brenis officially forbidding that practice among the Verkieri.
Julen planned to have Cohen poison the person Ambress would drink from before their duel to weaken him.
Vera was a poison expert living alone in the marshes who was preparing a ritual to strengthen the poison meant for Ambress.
Cohen and Julen found Vera dead at an old pagan shrine after she went alone to find something to protect Julen from the poison.
Julen revealed that he himself was meant to be the poisoned victim whose blood Ambress would drink before the duel, intending for both himself and Ambress to die.
Ambress forced Julen to kneel and beg for the honor of having his blood drunk, humiliating him repeatedly.
Using Vera's notes, Cohen completed the poison ritual and forced Julen to drink the mixture, binding the poison to his blood.
At the duel, Ambress drank Julen's poisoned blood after Cohen refused to drink first and insulted Ambress's manners.
Weakened by the poison, Ambress was defeated by Cohen, who then drank his blood.
Drinking Ambress's blood pulled Cohen's consciousness into Anahora, the dimension from which the corruption creating Verkieri originated and where Verkieri souls go after death.
In Anahora, Ambress's spirit begged Cohen to carry his soul back into the living world, since living Verkieri can host echoes of other Verkieri's essence.
Anahora is ruled by a nameless entity that Verkieri fear more than humans fear Satan, and after death Verkieri souls wander cursed plains under its gaze.

Cohen suspects Anahora is the world depicted on the blasphemous banner in Lazla's church, showing a three-eyed fanged figure devouring Verkieri and their victims, and theorizes it may be the same being Leonuka bargained with.
Cohen chose to leave Ambress's soul trapped in Anahora rather than carry it back.
After killing Ambress, Cohen found a report revealing that a new female Verkier had appeared near the northeastern wall of Svartra.
Cohen buried Julen Codrin's body beside a mountain monastery.
Anka found a manuscript describing the Impluvium vite, or Font of Life, said to grant anyone who enters it strength greater than Achilles.
Cohen and Anka searched for the Font of Life using clues from an old monk's diary, discovering ancient ruins in the mountains.
To enter the Font of Life, Cohen had to pass warrior's trials without armor, marked with magical symbols painted by Anka.
The trials included revenants, deadly traps, and a statue that flayed Cohen's arm to test his willingness to sacrifice.
Anka revealed that the Font of Life not only strengthens but restores youth, and admitted she is twenty years older than Cohen.
Anka wanted to use the Font of Life to become young again and start over, free of the darkness she let into herself through occult dealings.
Cohen and Anka defeated mummified undead guardians who had failed the font's trials before them.
There was only enough power in the Font of Life for one person, so Anka let Cohen drink from it instead of herself.
After drinking from the font, Cohen felt all his exhaustion and pain vanish, gaining renewed strength.
Cohen and Anka became romantically involved that night after leaving the font.
Farcus Derrescu, a servant of the boyer Bakir, secretly wanted his master dead and approached Cohen for help.
Bakir hosted a monthly contest called the lunar tournament (or 'rat race') inside a ruined fortress, where contestants wore animal masks.
Farcus offered Cohen entry into the tournament as 'the moth' so Cohen could get close enough to Bakir to kill him.
Farcus is the true heir to the title of Bandrescu and wanted an amethyst family ring from Bakir's treasury to prove his lineage.
Cohen won the lunar tournament by retrieving a coin swallowed by another contestant, the porcupine, cutting it from his belly.
As the winning contestant, Cohen was allowed into Bakir's treasury, refused to remove his mask, and asked for the amethyst ring, which Bakir claimed not to have.
Cohen fought and killed Bakir in the treasury after being denied the ring, then drank his blood and was pulled into Anahora.
In Anahora, Bakir, a sadist and masochist, welcomed torment rather than begging to return, but Cohen carried his soul back to the physical world anyway to deny him that satisfaction.
The amethyst ring recovered was engraved with demonic runes from Anahora rather than the Drescu family crest.
Farcus explained that Bakir killed most of his family but spared him and his brother Ducen, whom Bakir sexually abused and crippled after Ducen refused his advances.
Bakir promised Farcus the demonic ring could work miracles and might heal Ducen if Farcus impressed him.
Cohen gave Farcus the demonic ring despite warning him of its danger, out of sympathy for Ducen's suffering.
Farcus's journal later revealed the ring's ritual to heal Ducen failed, crumbling to ash, after which Farcus went mad and mutilated his brother trying to fix him.
Vicho is a Verkier collector of curiosities and forbidden knowledge who opposes Brenis's regime but refuses to join Cohen's war openly.
Vicho refuses to drink human blood and instead whips himself before a Christian cross, praying to be freed from his curse or granted death.
Vicho offered Cohen a protective amulet in exchange for help investigating the deaths of his friends D'vorah and Eli.
Vicho suspected he himself might have killed D'vorah and Eli during a blackout, as his hunger has grown harder to control with age.
At the crime scene, Cohen found a threatening note from Dr. Simeon demanding D'vorah and Eli repay a debt by week's end.
Dr. Simeon researched the plague and tried to synthesize medicine from Verkier blood properties, since Verkier blood cured disease including the Black Death.
Dr. Simeon had removed Vicho's fangs for research, though they eventually grew back.
Simeon experimented on living subjects, including himself, attempting to turn humans into Verkieri by driving a fang into the heart.
If the transformation into a Verkier is done imprecisely, the victim becomes a Muron, a mindless bloodthirsty abomination.
Dr. Simeon's failed self-transformation turned him into a Muron, and Cohen and Vicho were forced to kill him.
Vicho revealed that Simeon, desperate to avoid death, had once asked to be turned into a Verkier, but Vicho refused.
It was actually the transformed Dr. Simeon, not Vicho, who killed D'vorah and Eli during his mutation.
Cohen later discovered that Vicho, having lost control of his hunger, slaughtered a farm family who had known his secret, after Simeon had falsely blamed Vicho beforehand.
Realizing what he had done, Vicho chose to meet the sunrise and die rather than continue killing, and asked Cohen to stay with him until dawn.
Sara, the manumit woman who had once betrayed Cohen into a trap, returned to tell him the manumits would vote on his membership.
Cohen was voted into the Manumits, a group opposing Verkieri tyranny, with only Dro voting against him.
Craig, leader of the Manumits, tasked Cohen with finding four missing manumit scouts after suspecting betrayal by a member named Lios.
Cohen found a manumit scout named Buen dying, who revealed the Verkieri were constructing an army of artificial winged creatures rather than recruiting soldiers.
Buen's dying message included the code word 'Teayotim,' which referred to the ruined Church of St. Teotim in the Midens.
At the Church of St. Teotim, Cohen and Sara were ambushed by a gigantic winged creature made from a mutilated human body sealed inside a clay vessel.
Cohen defeated the gargoyle creature, discovering it was constructed from an amputated human body baked inside clay, with wings and bony scythe-like limbs attached.
Sara was mortally wounded by the gargoyle, and Craig killed her himself rather than let her fall into Kinaz Brenis's hands.
Craig told Cohen that if he were ever captured, Cohen should kill him too rather than let him be taken alive.
Inside the gargoyle's mouth was a manuscript written in an unknown language marked with an unfamiliar occult symbol, which Craig planned to have a rabbi named Measer translate.
